macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Wall Street futures rebound as oil retreats after fresh U.S.-Iran strikes
items.summary: U.S. stock index futures edged higher as oil prices steadied and investors weighed the impact of renewed U.S. strikes on Iran, which had reignited geopolitical anxiety and inflation fears. Reuters also said global markets were stabilizing after the latest escalation in the conflict.

items.title: U.S. stocks ended higher, led by a chip rally despite Iran worries
items.summary: MarketScreener reported that U.S. stocks finished higher, with semiconductor strength offsetting broader concern over the Iran conflict. The same update highlighted the Nasdaq 100 up 1.62% and the S&P 500 up 0.81% among the most mentioned moves over 24 hours.

items.title: Chip sector remains volatile as U.S.-Iran tensions and Samsung signals pressure the AI trade
items.summary: Reuters said U.S. semiconductor stocks were wobbling after renewed U.S.-Iran tensions and disappointing signals from Samsung Electronics rattled confidence in the AI trade. The report suggested the recent pressure on chip names may not be over.

items.title: Micron plans more than $250 billion of U.S. investment through 2035
items.summary: Reuters reported that Micron Technology will invest more than $250 billion in the United States over the next decade-plus, citing surging AI-driven memory demand and the Trump administration's push for domestic chip production. The announcement is one of the biggest company investment commitments in the latest market tape.

items.title: Fed held rates steady and signaled ongoing inflation vigilance
items.summary: A market recap from Brew Markets said the Federal Reserve kept its policy rate at 3.5% to 3.75%, with three policymakers dissenting and no one voting for a cut. The report framed the decision as evidence of a more aggressive anti-inflation stance.

items.title: Some Fed officials reportedly saw need for future rate rises
items.summary: The Financial Times said some Federal Reserve officials believed additional rate increases may be needed to contain inflation. That reinforces the market's focus on central-bank policy staying restrictive for longer.

items.title: IMF cuts 2026 global growth forecast, citing Iran war fallout
items.summary: Al Jazeera reported that the IMF lowered its 2026 world growth forecast to 3% and warned that the Iran war's energy shock is weighing on the global economy. The IMF said AI demand is only partly offsetting the hit from higher energy costs.

items.title: Japan 10-year government bond yield hit a 30-year high
items.summary: Reuters said rising oil prices and renewed inflation concerns pushed the benchmark 10-year Japanese government bond yield to its highest level in 30 years. The move also reflected investor concern about Japan's fiscal outlook.

items.title: China producer inflation accelerated to near a four-year high
items.summary: Reuters reported that China's producer price inflation rose for a fourth straight month in June, reaching its highest level since July 2022, while consumer prices also increased. The data points to persistent cost pressure for manufacturers.

items.title: Several large companies delivered notable earnings beats and guidance updates
items.summary: Brew Markets said GE HealthCare, Ford, Rocky Brands, Seagate Technology, and Mondelez all posted strong results or raised outlooks, helping some individual stocks outperform. The update specifically noted GE HealthCare rising after beating estimates and reaffirming guidance, Ford lifting its 2026 forecast, and Seagate benefiting from AI demand.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Work for workplace automation
items.summary: OpenAI unveiled ChatGPT Work, an agent inside ChatGPT designed to execute tasks across different applications and files, intensifying competition in professional AI tools. The launch adds to OpenAI’s push into enterprise automation.

items.title: Meta releases developer access to Muse Spark 1.1
items.summary: Meta debuted developer access to its Muse Spark AI model and an upgraded version, positioning it more directly against Anthropic and OpenAI in AI model commercialization. The release expands external access to Meta’s AI stack.

items.title: OpenAI launches GPT-Live voice models
items.summary: OpenAI released GPT-Live, a new family of voice models that can listen and speak simultaneously in real time. The move signals continued investment in conversational, multimodal AI.

items.title: xAI launches Grok 4.5 for coding and agentic tasks
items.summary: xAI launched Grok 4.5, calling it its most intelligent model yet and targeting coding and agentic workflows. The release is part of the broader race to improve AI systems that can take actions on behalf of users.

items.title: Anthropic adds Ben Bernanke to its Long-Term Benefit Trust
items.summary: Anthropic appointed former U.S. Federal Reserve chair Ben Bernanke to its Long-Term Benefit Trust, an oversight body meant to keep the company aligned with its public mission. The appointment highlights governance and safety oversight as a competitive theme in AI.

items.title: OpenAI faces renewed copyright dispute in New York
items.summary: Newspapers including The New York Times asked a federal court to sanction OpenAI, alleging the company misled the court about whether it can search its systems for evidence tied to copyrighted training material. The case underscores continued legal risk around AI training data.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Xbox Game Pass adds new July 2026 games; Microsoft also faces fresh scrutiny over subscription growth
items.summary: Microsoft’s latest Game Pass lineup for July 2026 has been announced, while reporting from IGN says Xbox CEO Asha Sharma acknowledged the service has not grown as expected and remains far below earlier targets.

items.title: Halo Infinite removed from HCS esports ecosystem
items.summary: Insider Gaming reports that Halo Infinite is being pulled from the Halo Championship Series, raising questions about the future of competitive Halo.

items.title: FaZe eliminated early at the Esports World Cup
items.summary: Insider Gaming says FaZe suffered a surprise loss to OMiT, a challenger team, in a notable upset at the Esports World Cup in Riyadh.

items.title: Nintendo Switch 2 launch concerns continue after reported pre-order damage issues
items.summary: Game Rant reports that some customers say GameStop may have damaged Nintendo Switch 2 units during pre-order fulfillment, adding to the launch-day conversation around the new console.

items.title: Square Enix says Final Fantasy VII Ever Crisis will be removed from app stores in October 2026
items.summary: GameKult reports that Square Enix announced Final Fantasy VII Ever Crisis will be delisted from mobile app stores on October 7, 2026.

items.title: Call of Duty: Black Ops 6 to become a standalone game
items.summary: A report in the Russian gaming press says Activision is separating Black Ops 6 from the Call of Duty HQ launcher, allowing it to launch independently.

items.title: Epic settles dispute with Fortnite leaker
items.summary: VGTimes and VGC report that Epic Games reached a settlement with a former contractor accused of leaking information about upcoming Fortnite collaborations.

items.title: New Shantae game announced with a 2027 release window
items.summary: VGC reports that WayForward unveiled the next Shantae title at Anime Expo, with a release window currently set for 2027.

items.title: PlayStation disc policy backlash continues
items.summary: VGC says Sony has remained silent as the 'Don't Kill the Disc' petition surpassed 165,000 signatures, reflecting ongoing backlash over the company’s physical media direction.

items.title: New Phantom Blade Zero gameplay footage posted
items.summary: Insider Gaming reports that 60 minutes of Phantom Blade Zero gameplay were posted online in 4K at 60 FPS, giving fans a substantial new look at the action game.
